stem: A 38-year-old woman has had recurrent swellings of the lips and hands for several years and two episodes of severe abdominal pain. She has no wheals. Daily antihistamines did not prevent the swellings. You consider the causes of recurrent angioedema. (Provisional panel credits.)

items.new_info: C1-INH function is low and C4 is low, confirmed on a repeat sample.
items.rationale: Low functional C1-INH is the shared finding of HAE-1 and HAE-2, and C4 is usually low in HAE-1/2. Recurrent swelling, abdominal attacks, no wheals and no antihistamine response also fit HAE-1/2.
C1q is low in 75% of AAE-C1-INH and nearly always normal in HAE. A normal C1q makes AAE-C1-INH less likely but does not exclude it (25% normal; also normal with anabolic androgens).

items.new_info: C1-INH function, C1-INH protein and C4 are normal on two occasions, and her mother has the same swellings.
items.rationale: HAE nC1-INH has normal C1-INH and clinically resembles HAE-1/2; a family history supports a hereditary form. It is very rare and most patients have no mutation found, so a strong shift is debatable.

stem: A 6-year-old boy has had recurrent bacterial infections since infancy, including skin abscesses and two pneumonias. Growth is normal. You consider a phagocyte defect or a complement deficiency. (Provisional panel credits.)

items.new_info: He now has a liver abscess with Staphylococcus aureus and a lung infection with Aspergillus.
items.rationale: Catalase-producing organisms such as Staphylococcus are troublesome in CGD, and invasive Aspergillus is the leading cause of death in CGD. Phagocyte defects typically involve skin, liver and respiratory tract.

items.new_info: He has had two episodes of disseminated Neisseria meningitidis infection.
items.rationale: In C5-C9 deficiency the only consistent clinical problem is disseminated Neisseria infection, because MAC lysis is important against these thin-walled bacteria. Properdin and factor D defects give a similar picture, so +1 earns partial credit.

items.new_info: The skin abscesses contained abundant pus.
items.rationale: LAD causes failure of neutrophil recruitment and inability to make pus; infections show no pus. Abundant pus argues strongly against LAD-1.

stem: A 9-year-old girl has had recurrent episodes of fever with an urticaria-like rash, joint pain and red eyes since early childhood. Episodes often follow exposure to cold. Her mother had similar episodes as a child. (Provisional panel credits.)

items.hypothesis: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS, NLRP3 gain of function)
items.new_info: Her mother has progressive hearing loss.
items.rationale: Muckle-Wells syndrome and FCAS are dominantly inherited NLRP3 disorders with fever, urticarial rash, joint pain and conjunctivitis; Muckle-Wells also causes progressive deafness.

items.new_info: Genetic testing finds a gain-of-function NLRP3 mutation.
items.rationale: FMF is caused by MEFV (pyrin) mutations, whereas CAPS is caused by gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations. A disease-causing NLRP3 mutation explains the picture and makes FMF much less likely.

items.new_info: The attacks respond dramatically to anakinra, an IL-1 receptor antagonist.
items.rationale: CAPS is driven by excess IL-1 and responds to IL-1 antagonists such as anakinra. A response supports CAPS but is not specific, because IL-1 blockade also helps other IL-1-driven conditions such as severe gout.
